messages:
ash: Quick sync — we need to lock the performance bets for next quarter. Customer-driven asks + capacity budgeting. TL;DR: pick tradeoffs for throughput vs p95 latency and define canary gating metrics.

maria: yes. big ask from FinCustomer: sustained 100 qps per customer with p95 <= 120ms for chat-small models. they also want cost guidance.

kevin: the 100 qps with 120ms p95 is doable if we enable KV-prefetch + dynamic batching, otherwise we need more dedicated capacity.

ash: propose three options for OKRs+rollout: A) conservative: KV cache + modest batching (slo 120ms), B) aggressive: quant+kernel work + batching (slo 100ms target), C) capacity-first: reserve extra Dedicated GPUs for key customers (slo 90ms).

jonathan: need to quantify unit cost delta for each. rough numbers?

kevin: back-of-envelope: A -> baseline cost, B -> -30% tokens cost but +2-3 weeks infra work, C -> +40% infra cost but simplest on correctness.

ash: noted. can we define canary gating so PMs can pick without burning customers? e.g., safety net metrics and fallback.

kevin: suggested canary pass criteria:
```
metrics:
  - name: p95_latency_ms
    threshold: 120
    mode: max
  - name: tokens_per_sec
    threshold: +20% (vs baseline)
    mode: min-improved
  - name: output_regression_count
    threshold: 0.5% (measured on eval set)
    mode: max
duration: 24h stable with <=1% error blasts
rollout_steps:
  - 1% traffic
  - 10% traffic after 6h if stable
  - 50% after 24h
  - 100% after 48h
```

maria: output_regression_count needs a clear eval harness. perf-ci can we run that on a representative prompt set? :eyes:

perf-ci: running eval job now on fincustomer_prompts; earliest ETA 8h. will post results as a followup message.

jonathan: what about kernel selection risk? some models regress with fused-kernel path on small batch sizes. need a compatibility matrix per model.

kevin: yep. for plan B we mark 'fused-kernel' as opt-in per-model. default to slower kernel if regression detected.

ash: good. also call out operational SLAs: fallback policy to host-model-variant or region if latency increases >20% during rollout. deploy-bot can we ensure auto-fallback is enabled in the staging canary?

deploy-bot: auto-fallback set to enabled for canary-group 'perf-nextq'. will trigger if p95 increases by 20% for >5m.

maria: capacity ask for FinCustomer: they prefer Dedicated commit. propose a hybrid: start with A + Dedicated for first month, then move to B for marginal traffic.

jonathan: that mitigates risk and gives us data for quant. we should also record unit-cost per token during canary to validate the -30% claim.

kevin: agreed. I'll add a microbench job that reports cost_estimate_usd_per_k_token and latency distribution.

ash: prioritize next-week: 1) bench harness + cost job, 2) KV-prefetch rollout plan, 3) eval set for FinCustomer, 4) canary gating config. Owners: kevin(1,2), perf-ci(1,3), maria(4).

maria: will brief sales and customer success. they want an explicit commitment window for Dedicated pricing.

jonathan: one more item — define rollback playbook (who's oncall, who approves). we need a short doc attached to the canary ticket.

ash: noted. owners: sophia will draft rollback doc. cc @sophia

sophia: will do. draft by EOD tomorrow.

perf-ci: eval job finished: no regressions observed on the eval set (0.12% regression_count), p95 improved slightly in quantized path but variance high. attaching the job id: perf-2026-03-19-814.

kevin: result sounds promising. variance worry means we need longer stable window before 50% rollout. suggest extending 24h->72h for B.

ash: ok change accepted: B rollout_steps -> 1%, 5% after 12h, 20% after 72h if stable, then 100% over a week.

maria: will communicate the longer ramp to FinCustomer. they are okay as long as SLA is documented.

jonathan: final ask — add measurement for small-seq vs long-seq p95. some customers skew short, others long. report both.

kevin: will add p50/p95 for seq<=64 and seq>512.

ash: great. I'll convert this thread into a tiny RFC and add to the roadmap board. thanks all. :rocket:
